cards.headline: Second inspection: is it a second offense?
body: After a corrective order, the motel faces a proposed 15-day suspension.
cards.takeaway: Two citations do not establish a repeat-offense tier. Compare violations and sanction dates.
cards.design: Deep navy, large sanction notice at center. Contrast the earlier corrective order with the proposed suspension.

cards.headline: Same business, two different offenses?

body.text: The motel was ordered to fix a breach of facility and equipment standards.
This inspection concerns room and bedding hygiene, a different violation category.
Only prior sanctions for the same violation within the legal period count toward the repeat tier.

cards.takeaway: Compare both notices' cited violations before assigning a second-offense tier.
cards.design: Three vertically stacked document snippets: earlier finding, current finding, then the classification test.

cards.headline: Second offenses: 5, 10 or 15 days

body.text: Repeat breach of lodging facility or equipment rules
Repeat breach of room, bedding or bath hygiene rules
Second failure to report succession of the business

cards.takeaway: Each period applies to its own violation category under the lodging sanctions schedule.
cards.design: Three proportional horizontal bars on the same day scale; emphasize 15 days without implying universal penalties.

cards.headline: A first pricing breach can trigger suspension

body.text: From July 14, 2026, a missing front-desk rate list or charges above posted rates carry a first-tier five-day suspension.
Missing online rates and overcharges also start at five days. System errors or similar causes not attributable to the operator are excluded.

cards.takeaway: The rule covers missing rates and overcharges; the online exception depends on fault.
cards.design: Side-by-side reception rate notice and phone booking screen; shared five-day marker below both.

cards.headline: Does a May penalty count after the July change?
cards.note: Older sanctions excluded from new tiers
cards.takeaway: With no other qualifying violations or aggravating factors, September uses tier one: five days.
cards.design: One horizontal timeline from May to September; place a strong dividing line at July 14, 2026.

cards.headline: When does the repeat-offense year run?

body.text: The date an administrative sanction was imposed for the previous violation.
The date the same violation was detected again after the earlier sanction.
A three-year period applies to specified anti-prostitution violations when an authority seeks sanctions.

cards.takeaway: The usual one-year lookback runs from the prior sanction to detection of the repeat violation.
cards.design: Two dated calendar tiles connected by one measured line; place the three-year exception in a separate side tile.

cards.headline: The 2014 lodging appeal: why did it fail?

body.text: A repeat youth mixed-sex lodging violation followed an earlier administrative sanction.
The tribunal found a phone inquiry about possessing ID insufficient to verify age.
Current law may exempt cases involving forged or stolen IDs, or assault or threats, under set conditions.

cards.takeaway: The 2014 appeal was dismissed. Review today's exemption and fine restrictions separately.
cards.design: Historical tribunal ruling on left, present-day statutory exceptions on right; visibly separate the time periods.

cards.headline: A second citation may not mean a second offense
body: Check violation type, sanction dates and rule changes before assigning a tier.
cards.design: Minimal rest card with oversized second-offense wording and generous cream space; three small paths beneath.

cards.headline: Before a hearing, compare these four records
body: Read the proposed suspension and legal grounds in the current notice.
Check the earlier order for the violation category and sanction date.
Match the inspection findings against photos and correction records.
Separate evidence disputing the breach from facts supporting mitigation.
cards.takeaway: Lodging suspension orders require a hearing. Organize the issues before responding to the notice.
cards.design: Four large numbered steps on a vertical document-review route; show the two official notices separately.

cards.headline: Two sanction notices: what should you prepare?

body.text: Gather the earlier sanction, the current proposed or final order, and inspection or correction records.
ETHOS Administrative Attorney Office offers a free preliminary review of the tier and records to check. Opinion drafting and filing are paid separately.

cards.takeaway: Share your records for a free preliminary review of the issues and next steps.
cards.design: Balanced two-column layout: operator documents on the left, legally scoped ETHOS review on the right; no buttons.
